subject: Civil Engineering
title: High-Speed Rail
description: Learn High-Speed Rail in one minute.

hook.text: Japan's bullet train launched in 1964 at 130 mph. France's TGV hit 200 mph by 1981.

buildup.text: High-speed rail needs dedicated tracks — no freight, no crossings, no slow zones.

discovery.text: Slab track replaces ballast with concrete — smoother, stiffer, and maintenance-free.

twist.text: Above 180 mph, aerodynamic drag dominates. Tunnel booms shake buildings near portals.

climax.text: China built 25,000 miles of high-speed rail in 15 years — the world's largest network.

punchline.text: Trains beat planes on trips under 500 miles — if the tracks exist.

quiz.question: Why does high-speed rail require dedicated tracks?
options: High-speed trains use a different track gauge than normal trains
Shared tracks with freight and crossings create speed restrictions and safety risks
Dedicated tracks are cheaper to build than shared ones
